title: The Khalsa debates how to answer Lahore

blocks.text: Subeg Singh carries the plea into a Sikh gathering presided over by leaders of the Khalsa, where Bhai Taru Singh's martyrdom is first remembered with grief and anger. The sangat curses the Nawab's cruelty before anyone even considers the request for mercy.

Soon the Singhs become desperate to launch an attack on Lahore, debating disguise, night assault, and martyrdom as better answers than negotiation. Their first impulse is not softness, but a warrior’s instinct to avenge sacrilege and defend the Panth’s honor.
This page is therefore charged with communal energy and strategic debate. Mercy remains possible, but only after anger has been fully voiced and measured against Khalsa discipline.
